deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous folio 16r. Let z = z(g) be an analytic function, presumably the conformal map relevant to the cylinder-electrostatics problem. Riemann sets y = 1/sqrt(dz/dg) and y1 = z/sqrt(dz/dg), so y1 = z*y. Then:
(i) The Wronskian is y*y1' - y1*y' = y^2*z' = 1.
(ii) A Möbius change z -> (a z + b)/(c z + d) induces a linear substitution of (y, y1). With the normalisation 1/sqrt(ad-bc) the Wronskian stays 1.
(iii) y and y1 are two solutions of one equation y'' + p y' + q y = 0. Since the Wronskian is constant, p = 0 [my inference from Abel's identity; the page writes 'Dann drückt man p und q']. Hence y*y1'' - y1*y'' = 0, i.e. y''/y = y1''/y1 = -q.

This folio, line by line:
- 'Wir haben also im Wesentlichen die [Form der Gl.] aufgefunden': so we have essentially found the form of the equation.
- The key statement, with Z a generic solution (y or y1): (d^2 Z/dg^2)/Z = an algebraic function of g.
- In modern terms [mine], Z''/Z = -(1/2)*{z,g}, where {z,g} = z'''/z' - (3/2)*(z''/z')^2 is the Schwarzian derivative. The quantity is Möbius-invariant in z. So z is the quotient y1/y of two solutions of the linear ODE Z'' = R(g)*Z.
- Why R is algebraic, following the next page: the image domain is bounded by circles, so reflection in each boundary circle is a Möbius map. Hence {z,g} continues single-valuedly across the boundary. On the doubled surface (the Schottky double of the triply connected region outside three circles) it is therefore an algebraic function of the uniformising variable.
- Next page, also mine to connect: zeta is real on the three circles, infinite at three points, and takes each real value three times.
- The rest of the folio begins a methodological passage, a lecture-style draft: 'Die Methode. Man hat bisher nur solche Aufgaben gelöst, die sich direct durch Entwicklung [lösen lassen]'. That is, until now only problems solvable directly by series expansion have been treated. The sentence breaks off.

What the page serves: the problem of electric equilibrium on parallel cylinders with circular cross-sections, i.e. the conformal mapping of the region outside several circles. It is reduced to a second-order linear ODE whose coefficient is algebraic, with the mapping function obtained as a ratio of solutions.
errors: No error on this folio itself.
Previous folio, as transcribed: 'y d2y1/dg2 - y d2y/dg2 = 0' should read y*y1'' - y1*y'' = 0. This is probably a transcription slip.
Previous folio: the claim that the common linear ODE has p = 0 is not written out explicitly; it follows from the Wronskian being constant (Abel). The step is correct.
'Algebraic function of g' is asserted without justification on this page. It requires the reflection / Möbius-invariance argument, which is only implicit.

results.what: y = (z')^(-1/2) and y1 = z*(z')^(-1/2) have Wronskian 1 and satisfy y'' = R*y with R = -1/2 times the Schwarzian of z. The map z is the ratio y1/y of two solutions.
results.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative / linearisation of the Schwarzian equation; z as quotient of solutions of a 2nd-order linear ODE
results.usually_credited_to: Kummer (1836, implicitly), Riemann (hypergeometric lectures 1858/59), Schwarz (1869/1873), named by Cayley (1880)

results.what: For the mapping onto the exterior of circles (multiply connected circular domain), the Schwarzian-type coefficient Z''/Z is an algebraic function of the parameter.
results.modern_name: Schwarzian of a circular-domain (Schottky-type) map is algebraic/rational on the Schottky double; circular-arc polygon mapping via linear ODEs
results.usually_credited_to: Schwarz (1869/1873) for simply connected circular-arc polygons; Schottky (1877) for multiply connected circle domains

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft fragment of Riemann's Nachlass work on electrical equilibrium on circular cylinders, published posthumously in his Werke (1876), where the Schwarzian/linear-ODE approach for circular domains already appears. Historians (e.g. Gray) acknowledge Riemann's priority there. The page adds only drafting detail.
